high.title: US Stock Markets Close: Four Major Indices Rise Over 1% as Trump Announces Pause on Iran Attacks, Wall Street Catches "This Signal"
high.summary: US markets surged over 1% Monday as President Trump announced he ordered military forces to pause strikes on Iranian power plants for five days following "constructive dialogue." Despite Iran's subsequent denial of negotiations, Wall Street interpreted this as Trump's eagerness to end the war. The Dow gained 631 points (1.38%) to 46,208.47, while oil prices fell over 10% with Brent crude closing below $100 for the first time in two weeks. This development is crucial for Taiwan's export-oriented economy and semiconductor stocks, as reduced geopolitical tensions could stabilize global supply chains and energy costs, potentially benefiting TSMC and other major Taiwan tech companies.

high.title: Apple Products Go Full AI: Hon Hai, Compal, TSMC to Benefit as Next-Gen Entry iPad Ready
high.summary: Apple is preparing to launch iPad 12, the next-generation entry model expected this year, which will complete Apple's AI integration across all hardware products. The new iPad will feature A18 chip upgrade from A16, enabling Apple Intelligence support for the most affordable tablet. This development significantly benefits Taiwan suppliers including Hon Hai (2317), Compal, and TSMC. The upgrade represents Apple's strategy to maintain pricing while enhancing capabilities, contrasting with competitors facing cost pressures from memory price surges. For investors, this signals sustained demand for Taiwan's semiconductor and assembly capabilities.

high.title: Tesla Chip Manufacturing Plan Targets Taiwan Talent Hunt: Aims at TSMC and Other Top-Tier Core Engineers
high.summary: Tesla's "TeraFab" chip manufacturing initiative, with $20-25 billion investment for 2nm fabs, has begun recruiting senior semiconductor talent in Taiwan. The company targets process integration engineers with 10+ years experience in advanced node development, directly competing with TSMC (2330) for core technical personnel. This aggressive talent hunt reflects Tesla's serious commitment to challenging Samsung, Intel, and TSMC in advanced semiconductors. For Taiwan's tech sector, this creates both opportunities and risks - potential brain drain concerns versus validation of Taiwan's semiconductor expertise. The move could intensify wage competition and talent retention challenges for existing semiconductor companies.

high.title: Foreign Investors Withdraw NT$83.92 Billion Amid Panic Selling Pressure, Domestic Capital Comes to Rescue
high.summary: Taiwan stocks experienced massive foreign selling pressure with NT$83.92 billion outflows on March 23, as markets reacted to Trump's ultimatum threatening Iranian power plants. The Taiex fell 821 points to 32,722, though domestic institutions including government funds bought NT$22.61 billion, helping cushion the decline. The dramatic turnaround came after Trump's evening announcement to delay Iran strikes, causing Taiwan futures to surge over 1,000 points in night trading. This volatility reflects Taiwan's integration with global markets and foreign capital dependence. For fund managers, this demonstrates both the vulnerability to geopolitical shocks and the resilience of domestic institutional support during crisis periods.

medium.title: Berkshire Hathaway Invests NT$57.8 Billion in Taiwan Insurer's Parent Company
medium.summary: Berkshire Hathaway will invest 287.4 billion yen (NT$57.8 billion) in Tokio Marine Holdings, acquiring a 2.49% stake. Tokio Marine is the parent company of Shin An Tokio Marine P&C Insurance in Taiwan, holding 50.18% ownership. This strategic investment will involve reinsurance and M&A cooperation, marking Berkshire's latest move in Japan following earlier investments in major trading companies.

medium.title: Trump's Latest Statement! Taiwan Index Futures Surge Over 1,000 Points After 90-Degree Rally
medium.summary: Taiwan index futures experienced extreme volatility, opening low at 32,220 but surging to 33,624 (up 1,065 points) after Trump announced constructive dialogue with Iran and a five-day pause on military strikes. The dramatic reversal from bearish to bullish sentiment reflects market sensitivity to geopolitical developments and highlights the structural weakness in Taiwan's recent rally.

medium.title: Oil Prices Plummet 10% Breaking $100 Barrier, Stabilize at Opening as Trump Says "Oil Will Drop Like a Rock"
medium.summary: Oil prices crashed over 10% Monday, with Brent crude falling below $100/barrel for first time in two weeks following Trump's announcement of delayed Iran strikes. However, prices stabilized Tuesday as Iran denied negotiations and continued attacks. The volatility reached levels not seen since April 2022, with potential significant implications for Taiwan's energy-import dependent economy.

medium.title: NVIDIA's Huang: AGI Already Achieved, Three Factors Make TSMC Unparalleled Globally
medium.summary: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang declared AGI already achieved and praised TSMC's three key advantages: comprehensive technology beyond transistors, service-oriented culture, and most importantly, trustworthiness. Huang revealed Morris Chang offered him TSMC's CEO position in 2013, which he declined to focus on NVIDIA's vision. His strong endorsement reinforces TSMC's competitive moat and strategic importance in the AI ecosystem.

medium.title: Strong Moat to Welcome Five-Year Golden Growth Period
medium.summary: Power device manufacturer Strong Moat (2481) announces "55 Plan" targeting $500 million MOSFET revenue by 2030, representing multi-fold growth from current $150 million. The company benefits from AI demand explosion and geopolitical client transfers, with B/B ratio maintaining 1.2-1.4 levels and order visibility extending to second half of year.
